newsitem.title: ITALY: Banca Napoli savings shares suspended.
newsitem.headline: Banca Napoli savings shares suspended.

text.p: Banco di Napoli savings shares were suspended after they had risen the 10 percent bourse ceiling in early trading on the Milan stock market, dealers said.
The savings shares had opened up 9.7 percent at 775 lire, and were then suspended at 780 lire compared to 706.4 lire at Tuesday's close.
Dealers noted that December 20 is the last day for offers to be submitted to the Italian Treasury to buy the 60 percent of the bank which is on offer.
In November, the Banco di Napoli said that three Italian and three foreign institutions had expressed an interest in buying the Treasury's 60 percent stake.

Italian state-owned credit institution Mediocredito Centrale said it aimed to submit a formal offer while Treasury-controlled Banca Nazionale del Lavoro and partly state-owned insurer INA have expressed an interest in making a joint bid.
No foreign institutions have publically announced an interest in Banco di Napoli.
On Tuesday, INA confirmed that it was preparing a bid and it had authorised its executives to prepare an offer to buy the stake together with BNL.
Milan financial newspaper Il Sole 24 Ore reported on Wednesday that BNL was planning a merger with Banco di Napoli, with INA as a major shareholder in the merger bank.
